content.user_title: Research GitHub Issues and Code Examples
content.value_statement: Developers lose time searching scattered GitHub issues, pull requests, discussions, and code examples. This skill guides focused repository searches for bugs, dependencies, and implementation patterns.
actual_capabilities: Provides activation cues for GitHub issue, pull request, discussion, and code searches.
Lists common VoiceLite-related repositories and when to search them.
Offers search examples for whisper.cpp, NAudio, WPF, Inno Setup, and .NET.
Explains broad-to-narrow search strategies using labels, dates, states, and sorting.
Suggests troubleshooting steps when GitHub results are broad, missing, or irrelevant.
limitations: Does not include executable scripts or direct GitHub API integration.
Requires the user or agent to perform the actual GitHub search.
Repository examples focus on VoiceLite dependencies and may need adaptation.
Search quality depends on public repository indexing and query specificity.

use_cases.title: Debug Dependency Issues
use_cases.description: Search known issues, fixes, and maintainer comments for third-party libraries used by an application.

use_cases.title: Research Implementation Patterns
use_cases.description: Find pull requests, discussions, and code examples that show how teams implement a feature.

use_cases.title: Triage Packaging Problems
use_cases.description: Investigate installer and release issues by searching repositories for similar failures and fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Search for a Known Bug
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer has an error or symptom in one repository.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to search GitHub for [owner/repo] issues about [bug or error]. Start with closed issues, then summarize likely fixes and linked pull requests.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Dependency Discussions
prompt_templates.scenario: A team is comparing guidance across related dependencies.
prompt_templates.prompt: Search [repository list] for discussions about [feature or performance topic]. Group results by repository, maintainer guidance, and recency.

prompt_templates.title: Find Implementation Examples
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer needs proven examples before changing code.
prompt_templates.prompt: Search GitHub code and pull requests for [API or pattern] in [language]. Prioritize active repositories and explain reusable patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Trace a Fix Across Sources
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced investigation needs issues, pull requests, and releases.
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate [dependency] behavior by finding related issues, discussions, pull requests, and release notes. Identify the fix path and remaining uncertainty.

output_examples.input: Find NAudio memory leak reports related to WaveInEvent.
output: A summary of closed issues that discuss disposal patterns and event subscriptions.
Likely fixes grouped by version, maintainer comments, and linked pull requests.
Follow-up searches when results are broad or unrelated.

output_examples.input: Research slow whisper.cpp transcription with tiny models.
output: Relevant performance issues and discussions, sorted by activity and recency.
Common recommendations such as quantization choices, beam size changes, or attention settings.
Uncertainty notes when reports conflict or depend on hardware.

output_examples.input: Find WPF Dispatcher examples for background updates.
output: Repositories and pull requests showing thread-safe UI update patterns.
A short comparison of approaches and when each one applies.

best_practices: Start with issue titles, then add labels, dates, state filters, and discussion searches.
Prefer closed issues, merged pull requests, release notes, and maintainer responses.
Record repository, date, state, and confidence for each result before applying advice.
anti_patterns: Treating one old issue as authoritative without checking current releases.
Searching only code examples when the root cause is discussed in issues or PRs.
Copying implementation advice without checking language, version, and project context.

faq.question: Does this skill run commands?
faq.answer: No. The skill file only provides GitHub search guidance and examples.

faq.question: Can it search private repositories?
faq.answer: Only if the user or connected tool has access. The skill itself does not grant repository permissions.

faq.question: Which repositories does it focus on?
faq.answer: It highlights VoiceLite dependencies such as whisper.cpp, NAudio, WPF, Inno Setup, and .NET runtime.

faq.question: Can I use it outside VoiceLite?
faq.answer: Yes. Replace the repository names and search terms with your own project dependencies.

faq.question: Does it return current GitHub results automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides how an agent or user should search GitHub using available tools.

faq.question: How should results be evaluated?
faq.answer: Prefer recent, closed issues, merged pull requests, maintainer comments, and examples from active repositories.
